# Third-party RF lenses — Sigma / Tamron / Viltrox

**Dimension:** third-party RF-mount autofocus lens availability, timeline, and
lightweight/budget picks. Sources in [citations.md](../citations.md); terms in
[glossary](../glossary.md).

## The critical constraint: APS-C only (as of June 2026)

Canon long restricted third-party autofocus RF lenses — it forced unlicensed
makers (Viltrox, Samyang) out around 2021–2022
[[57]](../citations.md#c57). In **April 2024** Canon licensed the RF mount to
Sigma and Tamron — but **for APS-C (RF-S format) only**
[[53]](../citations.md#c53). As of June 2026 **no native full-frame third-party
autofocus RF lens exists, has shipped, or has been officially announced** from
Sigma or Tamron [[55]](../citations.md#c55)[[62]](../citations.md#c62)[[60]](../citations.md#c60).

This resolves a contradiction found during research: one aggregator
([[59]](../citations.md#c59)) listed Sigma's full-frame 50mm f/1.2 DG DN and
70-200mm f/2.8 DG DN as RF. Cross-checking Sigma's own RF page
[[62]](../citations.md#c62) and Canon Rumors [[55]](../citations.md#c55)
[[56]](../citations.md#c56) shows those lenses are **Sony E / Leica L only** —
the RF listing is an error or adapter entry.

## Timeline

| Date | Event |
|------|-------|
| 2021–2022 | Canon forces unlicensed Viltrox/Samyang RF AF lenses off the market [[57]](../citations.md#c57) |
| Apr 23, 2024 | Canon licenses RF mount to Sigma — **APS-C DC DN only** [[53]](../citations.md#c53) |
| 2024 | Tamron's first RF lens (11-20mm f/2.8) ships **Dec 12, 2024** [[52]](../citations.md#c52) |
| Nov–Dec 2024 | Sigma 16/23/30/56 mm f/1.4 DC DN RF primes announced; 30 & 56 mm ship Dec 5 2024 [[54]](../citations.md#c54) |
| May 2025 | Sigma states **no full-frame RF plans yet** [[55]](../citations.md#c55) |
| May 2025 | Canon (CP+) says it doesn't differentiate APS-C/FF in approvals; FF third-party AF expected within ~12 months, first not from Sigma [[56]](../citations.md#c56) |
| ~Sept 2025 | Tamron 18-300mm f/3.5-6.3 RF ships ($629, APS-C) [[61]](../citations.md#c61) |
| Dec 2025 | Viltrox RF rumors; anamorphic-only approval, no AF prime/zoom license [[58]](../citations.md#c58) |

## What third-party adds vs Canon RF-S

Canon's native RF-S line is thin (a handful of zooms, no fast primes). Sigma's
f/1.4 primes and f/2.8 zooms fill the **fast-aperture APS-C gap** Canon doesn't
[[53]](../citations.md#c53)[[54]](../citations.md#c54). They beat Canon on
aperture-per-dollar — but not always on lowest sticker price (Canon's RF-S
18-45mm is ~$299 vs Sigma 18-50mm ~$599) [[51]](../citations.md#c51).

## Counter-perspectives

- **Full-frame buyers get nothing (yet):** an R8/R6 II/R5 II owner has **zero**
  licensed third-party AF options today — only APS-C bodies benefit
  [[55]](../citations.md#c55)[[56]](../citations.md#c56).
- **Canon could re-restrict:** licensing terms are private and new; Canon has a
  history of enforcement [[57]](../citations.md#c57).
- **Not always cheaper:** third-party wins on speed/quality per dollar, not
  necessarily lowest price [[51]](../citations.md#c51).
- **No Tamron 90mm macro for RF:** the popular 90mm macro exists only for Sony E
  / legacy EF — RF macro shooters are limited to Canon's own RF 100mm f/2.8L
  (see [macro-lenses](macro-lenses.md)).

## Gaps and limitations

- Exact weights for several Sigma primes (30mm, 16mm) came from search snippets
  with one cross-attribution risk noted by the discovery pass — flagged; only
  the 18-50mm (300 g) is from Sigma's directly-fetched page
  [[51]](../citations.md#c51).
- "First full-frame third-party RF AF lens" status is fast-moving; some unlicensed
  Chinese-brand FF RF lenses were rumored/grey-market in 2026 but not mainstream
  retail — excluded as unverified [[56]](../citations.md#c56)[[58]](../citations.md#c58).
